key_insight: Efficient variational quantum circuit simulation requires jointly choosing representation, precision and CPU/GPU allocation for each workload.
engineering_relevance: Benchmark complete energy evaluations under accuracy, memory and core constraints rather than assuming one simulator or device is always fastest.
method: Compare gate-based statevectors, direct Pauli evolution and matrix product states.
Test molecular and spin variational Hamiltonian ansatze and hardware-efficient circuits across width, depth and precision.
Profile CPU/GPU and worker allocations while checking accuracy and memory use.
evidence_signal: In FP64 tests, matched NumPy Pauli updates accelerated two-layer full LiH by 3.45×, while a GPU delivered approximately 30× acceleration over 18-thread Aer for 28-qubit, four-layer TFIM.
watch_item: Results depend on implementation and workload: startup overhead, worker memory and entanglement-limited compression can change the preferred configuration.
paper_title: Efficient simulation of variational quantum circuits: representation, accuracy and CPU/GPU allocation
